difficultyReason: Single causal inference with one visible alternative. Correct answer rules out the alternative explanation (bad weather) for increased crop yields.
stimulus: Farmer Chen increased the amount of irrigation to her wheat fields this season. The wheat yield from her fields this year is significantly higher than last year. Chen concludes that the increased irrigation caused the higher yield.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Other farmers in the region also increased their wheat yields this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Weather conditions this year were generally similar to those of last year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wheat is one of the most common crops grown in the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased irrigation often requires significant upfront investment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Chen's fields were planted with the same wheat variety as in previous years.

explanations.correct: If weather conditions were similar between the two years, this rules out the alternative explanation that better weather caused the higher yield. Since the only major variable that changed was irrigation, the causal claim is strengthened.
explanations.A: Irrelevant — what other farmers did does not explain whether Chen's increased irrigation caused her higher yield.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — the commonality of wheat farming has no bearing on what caused Chen's yield increase.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — cost considerations do not address whether irrigation caused the yield increase.
explanations.E: Does not strengthen; if anything, it leaves open the question of whether yield would have increased anyway due to other factors.

difficultyReason: Simple causal inference where the correct answer rules out a rival cause (laboratory contamination).
stimulus: Researchers found elevated levels of a harmful bacteria in water samples from a coastal region. Since the region experienced an unusual algal bloom earlier this year, the researchers conclude that the algal bloom caused the bacterial increase.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Algal blooms typically last several months in coastal environments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Harmful bacteria can reduce the clarity of water in coastal regions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In nearby regions without algal blooms, water samples show no increase in harmful bacteria levels.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The researchers used standardized laboratory techniques for all water samples.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Algal blooms have occurred in this coastal region before this year.

explanations.correct: By showing that regions without algal blooms do not have bacterial increases, this rules out other environmental factors and strengthens the causal link between the bloom and the bacteria.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — the duration of blooms does not explain causation.
explanations.B: Irrelevant — the relationship between bacteria and clarity does not address causation.
explanations.D: Addresses methodology but does not rule out an alternative cause for the bacterial increase.
explanations.E: Weakens if anything — if prior blooms did not cause bacterial increases, why would this one?

difficultyReason: Direct causal claim with one alternative explanation. Correct answer confirms a load-bearing premise about the mechanism.
stimulus: A pharmaceutical company introduced a new medication to treat insomnia. Sales of the medication increased sharply within the first month. The company concludes that patients found the medication to be effective.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the company's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The medication was aggressively advertised on television and in medical journals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients who used the medication reported improved sleep quality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insomnia affects millions of people in the country.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The medication is more expensive than competing insomnia treatments.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Previous insomnia medications on the market had limited side effects.

explanations.correct: By showing that patients actually experienced improved sleep, this directly supports the conclusion that effectiveness drove sales, rather than marketing or other factors.
explanations.A: Introduces an alternative explanation (advertising, not effectiveness) and thus weakens the argument.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — market size does not explain why this medication sold well.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — price does not explain effectiveness or sales.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the side effects of previous medications have no bearing on this medication's effectiveness.

difficultyReason: Single causal inference where the correct answer rules out a confounding variable (time).
stimulus: A school introduced a new reading program. Students' reading scores improved significantly over the following academic year. School administrators conclude that the new program improved student reading performance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many schools in the country have adopted similar reading programs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The school's student population did not change significantly during the year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Control schools that did not adopt the new program showed no significant improvement in reading scores.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reading is considered an essential skill by most educators.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The school had attempted other reading interventions in the past without success.

explanations.correct: By showing that schools without the new program did not improve, this rules out the alternative explanation that scores improved simply due to student maturation or general trends, thereby strengthening the causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant — what other schools did does not prove this school's program worked.
explanations.B: Accurate but does not address whether the program caused the improvement.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — the importance of reading does not explain improvement.
explanations.E: Somewhat supportive but weaker than a direct control comparison; past failure doesn't prove current success caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Simple predictive argument where the correct answer confirms a key assumption about the mechanism linking the premise to the conclusion.
stimulus: A technology company released a new smartphone with an innovative feature. Tech reviewers praised the feature in early reviews. The company predicts that the new smartphone will sell very well.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tech reviewers' opinions have strongly influenced consumer purchases in the smartphone market in the past.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company spent millions on developing the innovative feature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smartphones are one of the most popular consumer electronics products.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many competing companies also offer smartphones with innovative features.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company has a history of releasing products that appeal only to tech enthusiasts.

explanations.correct: By confirming that tech reviewers' praise historically translates to consumer purchases, this strengthens the link between the positive reviews and the predicted sales success.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — development cost does not predict sales success.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — market popularity does not explain this specific product's success.
explanations.D: Introduces a competitive threat and weakens the prediction.
explanations.E: Weakens if anything — a history of niche appeal contradicts the prediction of high sales.

difficultyReason: Single causal inference where the correct answer rules out an alternative explanation (pre-existing health difference).
stimulus: A fitness center claims that their new exercise program causes significant weight loss. They point out that members who completed the program lost an average of 15 pounds.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Weight loss is important for overall health.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Members who did not complete the program gained weight on average.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The exercise program is offered at multiple locations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exercise programs are becoming increasingly popular nationwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Many fitness centers offer similar weight-loss programs.

explanations.correct: By showing that non-completers gained weight, this rules out the alternative that participants would have lost weight anyway due to other lifestyle factors, strengthening the causal claim about the program.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — the importance of weight loss does not prove the program causes it.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — the number of locations does not prove efficacy.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — overall trends do not explain this program's effectiveness.
explanations.E: Introduces the idea that other programs exist but does not strengthen the causal claim.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal argument where the correct answer bridges a key assumption about how the cause produces the effect.
stimulus: A museum installed brighter lighting in its ancient artifacts exhibit. Museum staff observed that visitor attendance in the exhibit increased by 20 percent. The museum concludes that the brighter lighting caused the increase in attendance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brighter lighting reduces eyestrain for visitors viewing artifacts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ancient artifacts are popular attractions in museums worldwide.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lighting installation was completed during the summer tourist season.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other exhibits in the museum also received new lighting installations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Attendance at other museums remained stable during the same period.

explanations.correct: By showing that the brighter lighting improves the visitor experience, this supports the mechanism by which lighting would cause increased attendance.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — popularity in general does not explain this specific lighting change.
explanations.C: Introduces a confounding variable (seasonal tourism) that weakens rather than strengthens.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — other exhibits' lighting does not explain the artifacts exhibit's attendance increase.
explanations.E: Supports the argument somewhat but is weaker than confirming the mechanism.

difficultyReason: Causal inference with a visible alternative (pre-existing preference). Correct answer rules out this alternative.
stimulus: A restaurant introduced a new organic menu option. Orders of the organic menu items increased significantly in the weeks following the introduction. The restaurant manager concludes that the availability of organic options caused the increase in orders.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Organic foods are generally more expensive than conventional foods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the organic menu was introduced, customers had not requested organic options.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many restaurants in the city offer organic menu items.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organic menu items are prepared by the same kitchen staff as conventional items.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The restaurant's total number of customers decreased during the same period.

explanations.correct: By showing that customers had not previously requested organic options, this rules out the alternative that existing demand caused the orders, strengthening the conclusion that the availability itself caused the increase.
explanations.A: Accurate but raises the question of why customers would pay more; does not strengthen.
explanations.C: Introduces competitive alternatives that would weaken the causal claim.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — preparation methods do not explain demand.
explanations.E: Weakens the argument — if total customers decreased, the organic orders increase seems anomalous.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim with one obvious alternative. Correct answer rules out the alternative (timing coincidence).
stimulus: A government agency began a campaign to encourage citizens to conserve water. Two months after the campaign launched, water consumption in the city decreased by 10 percent. The agency claims that the campaign caused the reduction.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the agency's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water conservation is important for environmental sustainability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Similar campaigns in other cities did not result in measurable decreases in water consumption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neighboring cities that did not run conservation campaigns showed no decrease in water consumption.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The campaign included both television and radio advertisements.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Water rates in the city had remained stable for the preceding year.

explanations.correct: By showing that neighboring cities without the campaign did not experience decreased consumption, this rules out the alternative explanation that the decrease was due to external factors like drought or seasonal changes.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — the importance of conservation does not prove the campaign caused the reduction.
explanations.B: Introduces doubt about the campaign's effectiveness and weakens the claim.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the media used does not address causation.
explanations.E: Accurate but does not address whether the campaign (rather than rate changes) caused the decrease.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal argument where the correct answer confirms that the proposed mechanism actually produces the effect.
stimulus: A language school changed its teaching method from grammar-focused instruction to conversation-based practice. Students' spoken fluency scores improved significantly on standardized tests administered six months later. The school attributes the improvement to the new teaching method.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the school's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grammar is an important component of language learning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversation-based practice provides more opportunities for students to produce spoken language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many other language schools also use conversation-based teaching methods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Students' written grammar scores did not change significantly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Standardized language tests have been used for decades.

explanations.correct: By confirming that conversation-based practice provides more opportunities for producing spoken language, this supports the mechanism by which the new method would improve spoken fluency.
explanations.A: Accurate but does not explain why conversation-based practice would improve spoken fluency.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — what other schools do does not prove this school's method caused the improvement.
explanations.D: Consistent with the argument but does not strengthen the causal claim.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the history of testing does not address the new method's effectiveness.
